analysis.title: Metals sell-off runs ahead of physical markets
key_insights: Metals fell sharply in the week to 20 Nov 2026: copper down more than 8%, aluminium almost 6%, gold around 9%, on a stronger dollar, higher rate expectations and weaker risk appetite.
ING reads the speed of the sell-off as a repricing of investor exposure rather than a broad weakening in physical markets, which remain tight.

Copper is on track for one of its steepest weekly declines in a decade. LME and COMEX net speculative length have fallen sharply from recent highs, and positioning across the wider metals complex is less bullish.

Copper's correlation with equities, including AI-related stocks, has risen. As investors cut AI-related exposure, copper has become more vulnerable to the same selling. ING says copper demand does not depend on data centres alone, since grid investment and electrification are also demand sources.

China physical copper is tight: Shanghai inventories are at their lowest since late 2023 and the Yangshan premium hit a record $500/t this week. ING expects this to support prices once investor selling eases.

Some US copper is being offered to buyers in China (per Bloomberg). Volumes are limited so far, but metal stockpiled in the US ahead of potential tariffs could return to the global market, which would ease regional tightness if tariff expectations fade further.
Copper could stay under pressure if funds keep cutting positions or the macro backdrop worsens.

Aluminium nearby supply remains tight: the LME cash-to-three-month spread is in steep backwardation and LME stocks are historically low and largely of Russian origin. ING says this should contain near-term downside.

Aluminium medium-term outlook is weaker: Middle Eastern production is recovering and new Indonesian capacity is coming online. ING expects a surplus next year, which limits scope for a sustained price recovery.
Gold has fallen five straight sessions and is down around 9% this week, the steepest weekly decline since March, touching its lowest level since September 2025.
ING expects gold to stay vulnerable while rate expectations and the dollar remain elevated. The equity sell-off may have prompted some investors to sell gold to raise cash.
Central bank demand is a longer-term support for gold: China added 26 tonnes to its reserves in October. ING says macro forces will set direction for now.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term physical tightness in copper and aluminium should cushion the sell-off, but positioning unwinds and macro pressure can extend it. Aluminium faces a surplus next year.
